title: Star rating input and display
when: The user wants people to rate something from 1 to 5 stars, or to show an average rating.
inputs: whether half values show in display mode
prompt:
Goal: A rating input made of real radio buttons, with hover preview, and a read only display that states the value in text.
Steps:
1. <fieldset> with <legend>Your rating</legend> and five <input type="radio" name="rating" value="1..5">, each with a label holding visually hidden text 1 star to 5 stars and a star SVG with aria-hidden="true".
2. Fill stars up to the checked one with :has() or a row-reverse order and sibling selectors; hover previews the same way.
3. Arrow keys change the value natively; style :focus-visible on the star of the focused input.
4. Offer a No rating choice or a Clear button when a rating is optional.
5. Display mode is not a form: text 4.5 out of 5 from 120 reviews, with stars drawn by a width percentage on an overlay, aria-hidden.
Quality bar:
- Stars are at least 32 px apart on touch screens.
- The chosen value is clear without color.
- The average shows one decimal.
Pitfalls:
- Clickable spans with no keyboard access.
- Star characters read aloud as text.
- A display rating built from disabled radios.
Verify:
- [ ] Each radio has a label.
- [ ] SVG stars are aria-hidden.
- [ ] Arrow keys change the rating.
- [ ] Display mode states the value in text.
Output: Rating markup, rating.css, and rating.js only if the value is used live.

examples.input: avaliacao de 1 a 5 estrelas no formulario de review
examples.output: fieldset Your rating, five radios with hidden labels and SVG stars, display "4.6 out of 5 from 87 reviews"
